catapult.title: Hit Right Side of Arm Near Pivot
catapult.principle: Placing the red ball on the right half of the catapult arm (x≈0.5–0.9), near but right of the pivot, produces the optimal torque ratio that launches the green ball with sufficient rightward and upward velocity to reach the basket. Too far right (x>1.0) causes the arm geometry to shift unfavorably, sending green ball left or short. Too far left misses the arm entirely.
catapult.when_to_apply: When choosing the x-coordinate for the red ball drop, target x in [0.5, 0.9] to strike the catapult arm's right section for a rightward green ball launch.

catapult.title: Use Large Radius for Sufficient Launch Energy
catapult.principle: A larger red ball radius (1.3–1.5) delivers more impulse to the catapult arm due to greater mass and contact area, giving the green ball enough horizontal range to reach the basket at x≈3.5–3.7. Smaller radii (≤1.1) consistently fell short, with green landing at x≈2.3–2.6 instead of x≈3.2–3.7.
catapult.when_to_apply: When partial simulations show green ball landing short of the basket (x<3.0), increase the red ball radius toward 1.3–1.5 rather than adjusting position alone.

catapult.title: Drop From Moderate Height Above Arm
catapult.principle: Dropping from y≈-0.5 to y≈+0.2 (just above the arm) provides adequate impact velocity without overshooting into an unstable collision angle. Too high (y>1.0) causes excessive vertical velocity that over-rotates the arm, sending green ball into walls or ceiling rather than on a rightward arc toward the basket.
catapult.when_to_apply: Set y between -0.5 and +0.3 when targeting the catapult arm; avoid y>1.0 which consistently caused green ball to overshoot vertically in failures.

catapult.title: Verify Green Ball Reaches Basket X Range
catapult.principle: Use simulate_partial at step ~300–400 to check green ball x-position before committing to a full simulation. If green ball x < 3.0 at rest, the placement is insufficient. The basket x is approximately 3.5–3.7 depending on the seed, so green ball must reach at least x≈3.2 to have contact.
catapult.when_to_apply: After each placement candidate, run simulate_partial to ~step 400 and confirm green ball final x > 3.0 before calling simulate_action.

catapult.title: Avoid Alternative Strategies (Knocking Blue Ball)
catapult.principle: Attempts to knock the blue ball leftward out of the basket (by dropping red on the basket area or right ledge) consistently fail because the green ball lands far left (x<2.7) while blue ball, even if displaced, cannot travel far enough left to meet it. The geometry separating the two balls is too large for indirect contact strategies.
catapult.when_to_apply: Do not use red ball placements at x>2.0 targeting the basket or blue ball; always use the catapult arm mechanism to send green ball rightward toward blue ball.

catapult.title: Iteratively Fine-Tune X Position for Range
catapult.principle: The green ball's horizontal range is sensitive to the exact x of the red ball on the arm. Incrementing x by 0.1–0.2 steps while monitoring partial simulation results allows systematic range adjustment. Seed 1 converged from x=0.8 (short) to x=0.7 with r=1.5 (success) by combining position and radius tuning rather than large position jumps.
catapult.when_to_apply: When green ball lands consistently short, make small adjustments to x (±0.1–0.2) combined with radius increases rather than large positional changes that risk hitting invalid placements or changing the arm contact dynamics.

catapult.title: Mid-flight Height Sampling via simulate_partial
catapult.principle: In seed 2 step 6, simulate_partial at t=160 revealed green ball at pos=(-1.610, -1.545) with velocity (3.532, -4.966) — rightward motion and near basket height — despite the agent concluding green 'always goes to floor'. The ball was actually traversing the right half of the scene at the correct altitude; the failure was in not recognizing this mid-arc crossing.
catapult.when_to_apply: Whenever green ball's final position is at the bottom wall, run simulate_partial at intervals of ~40 steps from t=80 to t=200 to check if the ball passes through the basket height (y≈-2.4 to -3.0) mid-flight before concluding the strategy has insufficient range.

catapult.title: predict_first_contact for Blue Ball Access Angle
catapult.principle: In seed 3 step 3, the agent correctly used predict_first_contact at (3.5, -0.5, r=0.5) to confirm a valid path to blue_ball (contact at step 37, speed 1.07) with a nearly vertical approach normal (0.042, 0.999). This identifies that approaching blue from directly above is geometrically unobstructed, whereas lateral approaches at y<-1.5 are blocked by basket/ledge geometry.
catapult.when_to_apply: Use predict_first_contact with x near the basket center (3.3–3.7) and y between -0.5 and 1.5 to map out which approach angles reach blue_ball directly; prefer placements where the contact normal has a significant horizontal component to impart leftward velocity on blue.

catapult.description: Agent persists with catapult strikes for 10+ steps without verifying that green ball ever reaches basket height (y≈-2.4) during its arc.
catapult.why_it_happens: The agent fixates on green ball's final resting position (y=-4.78, bottom) and concludes 'green goes to floor', never checking whether the ball passes through the target height mid-flight before bottoming out.
catapult.how_to_avoid: Use simulate_partial at multiple timesteps to find when green ball's y-coordinate crosses the basket height (≈-2.4), then check the x-coordinate at that moment to evaluate whether horizontal reach is sufficient — do this before declaring an approach infeasible.

catapult.description: Agent rapidly cycles through unrelated strategies (catapult → knock blue leftward → hit green directly → deflector) without converging on any one approach.
catapult.why_it_happens: Each failed simulation is treated as evidence that the strategy is fundamentally wrong rather than incorrectly parameterized, triggering premature strategy abandonment.
catapult.how_to_avoid: When a strategy produces the closest result so far (e.g., seed 4's first placement giving +4.12 x-displacement), commit to it and systematically vary only one parameter at a time (x offset, height, radius) to maximize green ball's horizontal reach before switching strategies.

catapult.description: Agent attempts to knock blue ball leftward without first establishing where green ball will be when blue arrives — the two balls have no convergence point.
catapult.why_it_happens: The agent reasons about each ball's motion independently rather than computing the spacetime intersection required for contact.
catapult.how_to_avoid: Before trying to redirect blue ball, run a baseline catapult simulation and record green ball's position and time at several waypoints; then design the blue-ball deflection to aim blue toward that specific location at that timestep.

catapult.description: Agent repeatedly tries placements in the basket/ledge region (x≈2.5–3.5, y≈-1.0 to -1.5) that are consistently INVALID due to overlap with existing objects.
catapult.why_it_happens: The agent does not model the geometry of the ledge and basket occupying that volume, so it keeps guessing coordinates in that zone.
catapult.how_to_avoid: After an INVALID placement in a region, treat that entire vicinity as blocked and use predict_first_contact starting from higher y-values (y>0) over the same x-range to find the first valid approach path from above.

catapult.description: Agent treats the catapult as a simple lever and assumes more drop height or larger radius always increases rightward launch of the green ball, without noticing the arm's rotation direction and the ceiling blocker constraint.
catapult.why_it_happens: The agent assumes force magnitude monotonically increases range, ignoring that the black ball ceiling and arm rotation geometry can clip or redirect the trajectory regardless of impact energy.
catapult.how_to_avoid: Before scaling up impact parameters, use simulate_partial to verify the rotation direction of the arm at contact and check whether the green ball's apex stays below the ceiling blocker; if green hits the ceiling, reduce launch energy or shift the contact point along the arm.
